claims.head: Like for like: Dach against Klapka
claims.call: The Oilers’ L4 (Frederic, Dach and Howard) spends at least 47% of its 5-on-5 time against the Flames’ fourth line.
claims.body: At home, the Oilers keep sending Dach’s line (Frederic, Dach and Howard) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Babcock keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Flames’ fourth line is Othmann, Castagna and Klapka.

claims.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
claims.body: On the power play, Edmonton is the league’s best, but Calgary is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Flames take could cost them. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

notes.text: Samuel Honzek is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Yegor Sharangovich has taken his spot beside Mikael Backlund and Joel Farabee.
Maxim Tsyplakov has been a scratch for the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Joel Hanley has been a scratch for the last 10 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Jake Middleton has taken his spot beside Zayne Parekh.
Connor Zary has not dressed for the last 8 games.
Ben Jones was added to the roster on Oct 21 and has played beside Joel Farabee and Matt Coronato.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, up from 2% last season.
Zach Hyman is on injured reserve (neck injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin.
Mattias Ekholm is expected back after missing 2 games.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 43% of the team’s power-play time in 12 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 10 games, down from 30% last season.

EDM.head: The Oilers should be in control
EDM.body: Even though Edmonton will be without Hyman, the Oilers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. If the Flames want to spoil it, start with keeping dangerous shots away.

CGY.head: A steep climb for the Flames
CGY.body: Even though Edmonton will be without Hyman, the Oilers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Flames’ best hope is keeping dangerous shots away, plus a big night in goal.

story.head: McDavid’s favorite opponent
paras: The Oilers are 8-2-2. The Flames have won four straight.
At home, Mike Babcock likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Flames’ fourth line. The Oilers’ power play bites, but the Flames’ doesn’t.

items.text: Connor McDavid has a point in seven straight games against Calgary, and 15 points in his last nine against them.
The Flames have been without Samuel Honzek, Maxim Tsyplakov, Joel Hanley and Connor Zary for several games.
The Oilers are newly without Zach Hyman, and have had to make do without Matt Savoie all season.
Mattias Ekholm has missed the Oilers’ last two games.
